statements.text: The rate of Chinese advancement in the field of semiconductors is another threat to U.S. national security, and we are now in a global race to dominate the chip industry and must explore all options to curb Chinese dominance in semiconductor development.
statements.context: House hearing on CCP sanctions and semiconductor export controls, where the member questions a witness about China's chip acquisition and AI military applications.

statements.text: I bet it's a multiple of that number would be my guess. And, you know, I think that's true, actually, throughout its entire history. So when you talk about the escalating costs and the incredible innovation that's happening around AI systems, why is it that you suggest that the Federal Government needs to own a significant amount of the leading AI systems in order for America to compete?
statements.context: Question posed during a House Science Committee hearing on federal science agencies and AI in scientific discovery.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) has extraordinary potential to benefit society. It also has peril. The safe use of AI can lead to life-changing breakthroughs in medicine and science, but unsafe use can result in bias and discrimination, exacerbating existing inequities in society, and in the wrong hands can present a threat to society equal to that of chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear threats. [...] To promote the research and development of AI that will benefit everyone, I introduced bipartisan, bicameral legislation, the CREATE AI Act (Creating Resources for Every American to Experiment with Artificial Intelligence).
statements.context: Written prepared statement submitted for the record at a House hearing on federal science agencies and AI in scientific discoveries.

statements.text: AI will play a crucial and important role in our society and our economy in the coming decades.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Williams at a joint House Science Subcommittee hearing on federal science agencies and AI-driven discovery.

statements.text: And so what's happening in artificial intelligence is unlike anything else.
statements.context: Closing remarks by a member of Congress chairing a House Science subcommittee hearing on federal AI research infrastructure.

statements.text: Mr. Reynolds, as Congress looks to potentially regulate emerging technologies like AI, how should we try to ensure that small businesses can access and use AI applications that allow them to compete with a larger market participant?
statements.context: House Small Business Committee hearing on AI applications in financial services and housing, where the chair questions a witness.

statements.text: Some view artificial intelligence as dangerous and confusing, but you and your company have used it to turn something also confusing, like finding a house and obtaining a mortgage into a more simplified consumer-friendly process. Mr. Linda, how has Zillow used artificial intelligence to make the often opaque and stressful process of finding a home easier for consumers?
statements.context: House Financial Services Committee hearing on AI applications in financial services and housing.

statements.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman, and thank you all of you for being here, and I am a great supporter of innovation. I am a car dealer in Texas, and artificial intelligence has been at the forefront of innovation. Across all industries, AI has assisted in making business operations easier and less time intensive, including in the financial services industry, and AI provides increased workstream efficiency and improved client engagement. It is important for us to understand this evolution so that we may continue to make the practice of running a business more efficient and foster greater competition within industries.
statements.context: Opening remarks by Rep. Roger Williams at a House Small Business Committee hearing on AI applications in financial services and housing.

statements.text: I believe that AI can automate large portions of the intelligence cycle to improve efficiency, timeliness, and accuracy.
statements.context: Written responses to Senate Armed Services Committee advance policy questions for a nominee to be Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security.

statements.text:
As technology advances, predators are using AI to create deceptive material and exploit victims.

The TAKE IT DOWN Act will hold abusers accountable and empower victims of online abuse to have deepfake content or explicit material shared without their consent removed.

I look forward to sending this crucial legislation to @POTUS to be signed into law.

Today @POTUS signed the bipartisan TAKE IT DOWN Act into law.

This law will hold abusers accountable and empower victims of online abuse to have deepfake content or explicit material shared without their consent removed.

We will not tolerate the exploitation of our children.

Under the Biden Administration's Outbound Investment Rule, U.S. firms are now required to self-determine if a transaction might raise national security concerns without a clear guidance or a published list of restricted entities. This creates legal uncertainty, compliance risk, and could drive up the cost of doing business abroad. [...] Mr. Reissaus, if a Texas-based investor wants to put capital into a tech firm overseas to stay globally competitive, how do these new outbound rules impact that decision, and are we at risk of forcing American investors to sit on the sidelines where others move in?
statements.context: House hearing on U.S. policy on investment security, featuring questions to private-sector witnesses.

statements.text: As we talked about today, nearly half of small businesses are using the AI in some form, and more are exploring ways they could make their businesses more efficient. [...] The AI WISE Act directs the SBA to establish educational resources and online learning tools to help small businesses understand the benefits and risks of integrating AI into their operations.
statements.context: House Small Business Committee markup where the chairman speaks in support of H.R. 5784 before a voice vote to report it favorably.

statements.text: Evolving artificial intelligence tools are transforming the business world and reshaping how entrepreneurs and small businesses operate and compete.
statements.context: House Small Business Committee markup of H.R. 5764, the AI for Main Street Act.

statements.text: As AI becomes an integral driver of productivity and competitiveness across the economy, small businesses must not be left behind. Technology won't wait for small businesses to catch up, and Congress must help bridge that gap, to help close the innovation divide.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee markup, quoted in FedScoop

statements.text: AI tools are reshaping how businesses grow and enter capital markets.
statements.context: Speaking at a House Financial Services Committee hearing on AI innovation in financial services.

statements.text: [...] it is crucial that we ensure that AI is empowering rather than complicating the work of community banks. So, Ms. Manfra, what would we be thinking about to ensure that this technology can reach community bankers [...]
statements.context: Congressional hearing on AI innovation in financial services, where Representative Williams asks a witness about expanding AI access to community banks.

statements.text:
It is crucial that we ensure AI empowers, not complicates, the work of community banks.  

Today in @FinancialCmte, I asked witnesses how we can ensure this technology reaches local bankers and helps them better serve Main Street America. https://t.co/U6QFqJDeWL
statements.quoted:
WATCH: @RepRWilliams questions witnesses on how AI technology can help community banks grow and flourish:

“Artificial intelligence in the banking sector are two industries that are working together hand in hand. And for financial institutions, artificial intelligence is a valuable tool that allows them to navigate risk assessments and stress tests, detect and prevent fraud, assist with regulatory compliance, and several other critical operational duties. Now my district back home in Texas, Fort Worth, and around the metroplex and out west love their community banks who are the backbones of their communities. And as artificial intelligence continues to change the landscape of banking, it's crucial that we ensure that AI is empowering rather than complicating the work of community banks.”

📺⬇️

statements.text: Madam Speaker, we cannot leave Main Street behind in the adoption of AI. I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' on this legislation, and I yield back the balance of my time.
statements.context: Floor remarks by Rep. Roger Williams of Texas urging passage of the AI WISE Act.

statements.text: the AI for Main Street Act helps address this challenge by directing the SBA's Small Business Development Centers, or SBDCs, to assist small businesses in developing AI technologies into their operations.
statements.context: Floor statement in the U.S. House of Representatives urging passage of H.R. 5764, the AI for Main Street Act.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is changing how businesses operate in real time. [...] This bill directs the SBA to provide clear, accessible, and practical guidance that helps small business owners understand artificial intelligence in straightforward terms. It focuses on helping entrepreneurs evaluate whether an artificial intelligence tool is useful for their specific business, where it may fall short, and whether it is truly worth the cost before they spend their money to get that. Importantly, this bill does all of this without authorizing any new spending.
statements.context: Floor remarks by Rep. Roger Williams (R-TX) in support of H.R. 5784, the AI-WISE Act, during House debate.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to streamline operations, reduce costs, and boost productivity for small businesses. [...] As artificial intelligence becomes a core driver of productivity and competitiveness, Main Street cannot be left behind.
statements.venue: House floor speech on H.R. 5764, AI for Main Street Act

statements.text: This morning, I met with @TeamUVeye in my D.C. office to discuss expanding AI capabilities and how innovation can help small businesses succeed. https://t.co/LGFg41pXhA
Businesses across the country adopting artificial intelligence, which is reshaping how they operate, detect fraud, improve customer service, and process information.
statements.context: Markup hearing in a U.S. House committee where the chairman presents and votes on H.R. 8881, the Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026.

statements.text: The bill requires the SBA to evaluate both the benefits and risks associated with these technologies, identify appropriate uses for AI tools, and explain how the agency maintains human involvement and oversight in its decisions assisted by AI.
statements.context: Floor statement in the House of Representatives urging passage of H.R. 8881, the SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026.

statements.text: Mr. Speaker, I move to suspend the rules and pass the bill (H.R. 8881) to amend the Small Business Act to require the Administrator of the Small Business Administration to report on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning by the Administration [...]
statements.context: Floor debate in the House of Representatives on the SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026, a bill requiring the SBA to report on its AI and machine learning use.

statements.text:
Yesterday, I visited UVEYE Technology in Fort Worth, Texas.  

UVEYE is an AI-powered vehicle inspection company that uses high-resolution cameras, computer vision, and machine learning to inspect vehicles in seconds.   

It’s exciting to see American innovation continuing to shape the future of the automotive industry.

Today, I will chair a @HouseSmallBiz hearing on how artificial intelligence is shaping the future of America's small businesses.   

Watch live at 10:00 AM ET:
https://t.co/NvG8RKQjTX

Artificial intelligence has quickly transitioned from novelty to an indispensable business tool for Main Street businesses across the country. [...] Importantly, early data is showing that AI's rise is not coming at the expense of workers. In fact, eighty-two percent of small businesses using AI grew their workforce over the past year.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street'

statements.text: The Biden-Harris Administration took a heavy-handed approach to AI. On October 30, 2023, they released an Executive Order imposing sweeping regulatory requirements and compliance burdens that threatened to smother AI innovation before small businesses ever got the chance to benefit from it. [...] Europe chose to regulate first and innovate later, and today, their small businesses are falling behind. The United States cannot make the same mistake.
statements.venue: Opening statement, House Small Business Committee hearing 'AI on Main Street'

statements.text: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming one of the most valuable tools available to small business owners. [...] That's why this Committee and the Small Business Administration are working to expand the resources and educational opportunities Main Street needs to adopt AI with confidence, while ensuring unnecessary red tape doesn't stand in the way of innovation.
statements.venue: House Small Business Committee press release on AI hearing
